## Structure and components

- [statement] Builder classes and LINQ queries are not a security sanitization layer. Validate untrusted runtime field names and dictionary keys separately: the driver advisory describes keys being interpreted as path syntax while values are serialized as BSON values. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/crud/query/query-filter.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-csharp-driver/security/advisories/GHSA-2xqr-fxmx-2cmf

## How it works

- [statement] RegisterClassMap can explicitly define member mappings. Register a class map before it is needed; call AutoMap before adjusting individual members when combining automatic and manual mappings. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization/class-mapping.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] Chronicle demonstrates registering GuidSerializer(GuidRepresentation.Standard) alongside IgnoreExtraElementsConvention(true), and advises adding CamelCaseElementNameConvention only when its naming policy is configured for camel case. (low confidence) — https://github.com/cratis/chronicle/blob/c506441e3f87c709d2bc3671c9ac2ee73049b7ce/Documentation/client-snippets/get-started/mongodb/conventions.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation
- [statement] setOnInsert applies only when an upsert inserts a document; the documented invocation passes new UpdateOptions().upsert(true). (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/java/sync/current/builders/updates.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Java sync driver CRUD, Filters/Updates builders and POJO codecs
- [statement] find() returns a Cursor of matches; find_one() returns Result<Option<T>>, with Some for a match and None when no document matches. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/crud/query/retrieve.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] Serde rename changes the serialized and deserialized field name, and default supplies Default::default() when a field is absent during deserialization. These attributes customize Rust-to-BSON mapping in the driver. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://serde.rs/field-attrs.html

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Configure binary GUIDs explicitly. A common startup configuration is BsonSerializer.RegisterSerializer(new GuidSerializer(GuidRepresentation.Standard)); use BsonGuidRepresentation attributes for properties requiring a different representation. Chronicle independently demonstrates the same global Standard serializer configuration. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization/guids.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation · also: https://github.com/cratis/chronicle/blob/c506441e3f87c709d2bc3671c9ac2ee73049b7ce/Documentation/client-snippets/get-started/mongodb/conventions.md
- [statement] Configure a POJO collection by combining the default codec registry with a PojoCodecProvider registry, applying it to the database or collection, and passing the POJO class to getCollection(). (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/java/sync/current/data-formats/document-data-format-pojo.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Java sync driver CRUD, Filters/Updates builders and POJO codecs · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/java/sync/current/data-formats/pojo-customization.md
- [statement] Enable the blocking API with the sync Cargo feature and import types from mongodb::sync. The quick reference executes synchronous CRUD actions with run(), alongside async examples using await. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/runtimes.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-rust-driver, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/reference/quick-reference.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] C# MongoBulkWriteException exposes individual operation errors through WriteErrors and the write concern error separately through WriteConcernError. The typed exception inherits these properties. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo-csharp-driver/main/src/MongoDB.Driver/MongoBulkWriteException.cs · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Bulk write exception types and partial results in the C#, Java and Rust drivers · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-csharp-driver/blob/main/src/MongoDB.Driver/MongoBulkWriteException.cs
- [statement] Java getWriteErrors() is non-null but may be empty when a write concern error exists. getWriteConcernError() may be null; when it is null, the write-error list is nonempty. Inspect both channels when handling MongoBulkWriteException. (high confidence) — https://mongodb.github.io/mongo-java-driver/5.6/apidocs/driver-core/com/mongodb/MongoBulkWriteException.html · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Bulk write exception types and partial results in the C#, Java and Rust drivers · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo-java-driver/main/driver-core/src/main/com/mongodb/MongoBulkWriteException.java
- [statement] Rust represents an insert_many failure with ErrorKind::InsertMany(InsertManyError). This is the collection insert-many error variant to inspect within the bounded collection-write scope. (high confidence) — https://docs.rs/mongodb/3.3.0/mongodb/error/enum.ErrorKind.html · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Bulk write exception types and partial results in the C#, Java and Rust drivers · also: https://docs.rs/mongodb/3.3.0/src/mongodb/error.rs.html
- [statement] Rust InsertManyError does not publicly expose its inserted_ids map: the source declares that field pub(crate) and marks it with serde(skip), while the public API lists only write_errors and write_concern_error plus private fields. Applications cannot obtain that internal partial inserted-ID map through the public exception fields. (high confidence) — https://docs.rs/mongodb/3.3.0/src/mongodb/error.rs.html · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Bulk write exception types and partial results in the C#, Java and Rust drivers · also: https://docs.rs/mongodb/3.3.0/mongodb/error/struct.InsertManyError.html
- [statement] In Elsa issue 6001, the reporter traced an Expression not supported: x.Key failure during index creation to a read-only Key property omitted from the class map. The reporter proposed explicitly registering that property; this is a historical application report, not a universal current-driver failure. (low confidence) — https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/issues/6001 · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] Find supports FirstOrDefault and ToList materialization, including asynchronous forms. Fluent reads can chain Limit, Skip, SortBy, and Project. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/reference/quick-reference.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] Kevin Smith’s historical tutorial says LINQ lacks asynchronous methods. The official LINQ guide documents asynchronous iteration through ToAsyncEnumerable. Treat the tutorial’s async limitation as historical advice, not a universal constraint. (medium confidence) — https://kevsoft.net/2020/02/28/finding-documents-in-mongodb-using-csharp.html · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/aggregation/linq.md
- [statement] An unspecified binary GUID representation is an error: GuidSerializer throws BsonSerializationException when asked to serialize or deserialize binary GUIDs with GuidRepresentation.Unspecified. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-csharp-driver/blob/main/src/MongoDB.Bson/Serialization/Serializers/GuidSerializer.cs · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation
- [statement] The serializer registry is global to the application, and MongoDB documents that multiple serializer registries cannot be used in one application. Register custom serializers before their use. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation
- [statement] find_one distinguishes no match from an error through Result<Option<T>>: a matching document yields Some, and no match yields None. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/crud/query/retrieve.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] Read options can be chained directly before awaiting the operation; examples use sort, limit and projection. The retrieval guide cautions that earlier driver APIs instead construct an options object and pass it to the find method. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/crud/query/retrieve.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/reference/quick-reference.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Call AsQueryable() on a typed collection to compose LINQ queries; the driver translates supported LINQ expressions into aggregation operations rather than supporting every possible C# expression. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/aggregation/linq.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-analyzer/current/code-type/linq.md
- [statement] JAVA-6138 reports that generic hierarchy serialization that worked in 5.5.x failed in 5.6.x with a CodecConfigurationException for java.lang.Object while encoding a Map<String, Object> property. Treat this as a version-specific reported regression rather than a universal POJO limitation. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/JAVA-6138 · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Java sync driver CRUD, Filters/Updates builders and POJO codecs
- [statement] Serde rename changes a serialized and deserialized field name. The driver integrates Serde attributes into custom mapping, allowing a Rust field name to differ from its stored name. (high confidence) — https://serde.rs/field-attrs.html · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md
- [statement] For missing fields, Serde default uses Default::default(); skip suppresses both serialization and deserialization. These differ from custom serialize_with and deserialize_with field helpers. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/data-formats/serialization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] The driver README snapshot warns that dropping unfinished driver futures for cancellation or timeout can leave internal state inconsistent. It recommends polling them to completion and suggests timing out a spawned task’s JoinHandle instead of the driver future directly. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-rust-driver · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime
- [statement] Serde skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none" omits a None field when serializing. This is a conditional serialization rule, unlike skip, which suppresses both serialization and deserialization. (low confidence) — https://serde.rs/field-attrs.html · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Rust driver CRUD, serde mapping and async runtime

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The C# source defines MongoBulkWriteException<TDocument> as the typed bulk-write exception. Its Result property exposes BulkWriteResult<TDocument>, and UnprocessedRequests exposes the write models that were not processed. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo-csharp-driver/main/src/MongoDB.Driver/MongoBulkWriteException.cs · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Bulk write exception types and partial results in the C#, Java and Rust drivers · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-csharp-driver/blob/main/src/MongoDB.Driver/MongoBulkWriteException.cs
- [statement] Rust InsertManyError publicly exposes write_errors as an optional vector of IndexedWriteError and write_concern_error as an optional WriteConcernError, separating individual write failures from write concern failures. (high confidence) — https://docs.rs/mongodb/3.3.0/mongodb/error/struct.InsertManyError.html · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Bulk write exception types and partial results in the C#, Java and Rust drivers · also: https://docs.rs/mongodb/3.3.0/src/mongodb/error.rs.html
- [statement] Java MongoBulkWriteException represents bulk operation errors and exposes individual BulkWriteError entries through getWriteErrors(). The AWS guide independently demonstrates catching this exception around collection.bulkWrite() and iterating those entries. (medium confidence) — https://mongodb.github.io/mongo-java-driver/5.6/apidocs/driver-core/com/mongodb/MongoBulkWriteException.html · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Bulk write exception types and partial results in the C#, Java and Rust drivers · also: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/devguide/java-crud-operations.html
- [statement] Query filters select documents for reads, updates and deletes; Builders<TDocument>.Filter provides builder methods for those filters. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/crud/query/query-filter.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] Typed equality filters can be passed to Find; the query-filter guide also shows the equivalent lambda predicate directly in Find. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/crud/query/query-filter.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/reference/quick-reference.md
- [statement] The CRUD API exposes InsertOne and InsertMany for POCO documents, with asynchronous counterparts. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/reference/quick-reference.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] ReplaceOne accepts a replacement POCO and a filter; DeleteOne and DeleteMany accept filters, with asynchronous variants shown in the quick reference. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/reference/quick-reference.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] For LINQ diagnostics, ToString exposes the translated pipeline for non-scalar query objects. LoggedStages exposes it for scalar operations and must be read immediately after execution. LoggedStages is not thread-safe. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/aggregation/linq.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] A POCO collection uses an automatic class map that matches document field names to class property names; incompatible property and field types can produce deserialization exceptions. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization/class-mapping.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] Typed collections can represent BSON documents as C# objects. The driver uses a class map to serialize and deserialize those objects. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization/class-mapping.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping · also: https://kevsoft.net/2020/02/28/finding-documents-in-mongodb-using-csharp.html
- [statement] Filter builders and lambda predicates provide alternative ways to express equality queries passed to Find. Builder filters can also be composed conditionally. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/crud/query/query-filter.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping · also: https://kevsoft.net/2020/02/28/finding-documents-in-mongodb-using-csharp.html
- [statement] An empty filter matches all documents. Query filters select the documents that read, update, and delete operations target. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/crud/query/query-filter.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] Call AsQueryable on a collection to compose LINQ queries. The driver translates supported statements into aggregation pipeline stages, including Where into $match and Select into $project. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/aggregation/linq.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] Not every LINQ expression maps to a MongoDB query. The official guide lists unsupported Replace overloads that throw ExpressionNotSupportedException at runtime. (medium confidence) — https://kevsoft.net/2020/02/28/finding-documents-in-mongodb-using-csharp.html · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/aggregation/linq.md
- [statement] The version-three upgrade guide states that LINQ2 was removed and LINQ3 must be used for LINQ queries. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/reference/upgrade/v3.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] For client-side projections, the version-three upgrade guide documents ExpressionNotSupportedException by default and an opt-in through EnableClientSideProjections on TranslationOptions. These options can apply to an individual query or to MongoClientSettings. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/reference/upgrade/v3.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver CRUD with builders, LINQ provider and POCO mapping
- [statement] Register naming conventions by placing CamelCaseElementNameConvention in a ConventionPack and passing the pack to ConventionRegistry.Register; this changes serialized field names to camel case without decorating each member. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization/poco.md
- [statement] EnumRepresentationConvention selects enum storage representation; IgnoreExtraElementsConvention controls whether deserialization ignores extra document elements. These are separate serialization choices. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation
- [statement] GUID subtype 3 did not standardize byte order across drivers. Standard maps to subtype 4; CSharpLegacy, JavaLegacy and PythonLegacy map to subtype 3 with different byte orders. MongoDB recommends subtype 4 for new GUID data. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization/guids.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation
- [statement] For mixed historical representations across properties, combine a global GuidSerializer with BsonGuidRepresentation attributes on exceptional properties. The upgrade guide advises checking existing GUID representations before introducing a global serializer. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization/guids.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/reference/upgrade/v3.md
- [statement] The version 3.0 migration supports only GuidRepresentationMode.V3 semantics. BsonBinaryData(Guid) and BsonBinaryData.GuidRepresentation were removed; parameterless BsonBinaryData.ToGuid() is limited to subtype 4, while other representations require ToGuid(GuidRepresentation). (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/reference/upgrade/v3.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation
- [statement] Convention packs apply serialization rules without decorating every class. Register a ConventionPack through ConventionRegistry.Register(); the documented t => true predicate applies the pack to all types. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation · also: https://github.com/cratis/chronicle/blob/c506441e3f87c709d2bc3671c9ac2ee73049b7ce/Documentation/client-snippets/get-started/mongodb/conventions.md
- [statement] Built-in conventions cover camel-case element names, enum representation, ignoring extra document elements during deserialization, and allowed types for ObjectSerializer. - [statement] The serializer registry is global to the application. ObjectSerializer accepts an allowed-type predicate; the documentation demonstrates extending ObjectSerializer.DefaultAllowedTypes with explicitly permitted custom types and requires registering ObjectSerializer at program startup. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/csharp/current/serialization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, C#/.NET driver serialization conventions and GUID representation
- [statement] A November 2024 driver 3.0.0 upgrade report encountered "Expected BsonBinarySubType to be UuidStandard, but it is UuidLegacy." after registering Standard. The response attributed this to stored legacy GUID values and advised matching the default or property-specific representation; the official guide separately documents legacy byte orders and per-property configuration. - [statement] For direct BSON access to a C# legacy GUID, construct BsonBinaryData(guid, GuidRepresentation.CSharpLegacy) explicitly. The official GUID guide shows that value placed in a BsonDocument filter. - [statement] Filters provides static factories that produce BSON query filters usable by find, update and delete methods; the POJO CRUD example also uses Filters.lte and Filters.eq. - [statement] Automatic POJO mapping follows JavaBean getter/setter conventions and can access public fields directly. Quarkus independently documents the same PojoCodecProvider field/accessor model. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/java/sync/current/data-formats/document-data-format-pojo.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Java sync driver CRUD, Filters/Updates builders and POJO codecs · also: https://quarkus.io/guides/mongodb-panache
- [statement] BsonProperty customizes the BSON field name, BsonId selects the identifier property, and BsonIgnore controls whether a property is serialized or deserialized. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/java/sync/current/data-formats/pojo-customization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Java sync driver CRUD, Filters/Updates builders and POJO codecs · also: https://quarkus.io/guides/mongodb-panache
- [statement] POJO codecs call an empty no-argument constructor by default. With annotation conventions enabled, BsonCreator selects a different constructor or public static creator; constructor parameters require BsonProperty or BsonId annotations. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/java/sync/current/data-formats/pojo-customization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Java sync driver CRUD, Filters/Updates builders and POJO codecs
- [statement] Generic POJO properties require concrete bounded type parameters. ClassModelBuilder retains concrete type information to work around erasure; PropertyCodecProvider permits custom handling of generic property types. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/java/sync/current/data-formats/pojo-customization.md · keywords: MongoDB driver CRUD idioms in the C#/.NET, Java sync and Rust drivers, Java sync driver CRUD, Filters/Updates builders and POJO codecs
- [statement] Since driver 4.5 the PojoCodecProvider no longer supplies enum conversion itself; include an enum codec such as the default registry provider. Codec registries use precedence order, so a custom enum codec can be placed before the default registry. - [statement] Rust driver 3.0 removed async-std support; its asynchronous API requires Tokio. Guidance that offers both runtimes applies to the 2.x driver. - [statement] In driver 3.0, options can be chained directly onto an operation before awaiting it, replacing the older separate options argument; a session can also be chained. - [statement] Model stored documents with a custom Rust type deriving Serialize and Deserialize, and use that type as the Collection generic parameter. The driver serializes inserted instances through Serde. - [statement] The asynchronous cursor idiom is to await find(), then repeatedly await try_next(); the quick reference also shows try_collect().await to collect results. - [statement] Custom field conversion can use serialize_with and deserialize_with functions, or with to select a module supplying both operations. - [statement] Beginning with Rust driver v3.0, Tokio is the only supported asynchronous runtime. An async-std application can host a Tokio Runtime and spawn driver work on it, using the same Runtime instance for Client creation and operations.
